outlook: Soybeans led Monday's grain trade lower, with January futures down 17½ cents at $12.16¾ on harvest pressure, continued fund selling and a sharp drop in soybean oil and meal, despite new export sales including one to China. December corn finished nearly flat, up half a cent at $4.48¼, as USDA's 1.7 million-tonne sale to Mexico — the largest of the marketing year — offset fund liquidation and rain expected to slow harvest this week. Wheat edged higher from oversold levels after nine straight weekly losses in Chicago: December Minneapolis spring wheat rose 1¼ cents to $6.25 and Chicago wheat 3 cents to $6.06½, while January canola gained C$0.40 to C$788.40. Crude oil fell more than 7% on progress toward a U.S.–Iran deal; cash bids shown are still from Friday's USDA Minneapolis report.
